messages.subject: SEM non converging/
parts:
I want to study the causal effect of "TS" on "acquis". "TS" and "acquis" depend on "sexe_Fille" and "pcs_r". "TS" , "acquis" and "pcs_r" are ordinal variables and "sexe_Fille" is a dichotomous variable. I am unable to make my model converge. Here is the model :

data[, c("acquis",
             "TS", "pcs_r")] <-
  lapply(data[,c("acquis",
                    "TS","pcs_r")], ordered)
model <- '
niveau =~ acquis
 # Modèle de mesure pour la variable temps de travail
temps_travail =~   TS
 
# Modèle de mesure pour la variable sexe
sex2 =~ sexe_Fille
 
# Modèle de mesure pour la variable pcs
prof =~    pcs_r
 
# Modèle structurel
niveau ~ temps_travail + sex2 +prof
temps_travail ~ sex2 +prof
'
fit <- sem(model, data = data,ordered=c("acquis"  "TS", "pcs_r"),
           estimator = "WLSMV", std.lv=TRUE, control = list(maxit = 10000))

This is Warning messages :
Warning messages: 1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats, : lavaan WARNING: Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not identified. 2: In lav_object_post_check(object) : lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative


The sample size is large enough (12,000), there are no missing variables, and the assumptions of the model are robust. Can you please help me, as I am new to Lavaan and despite the documentation, I cannot seem to find the error?

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: SEM non converging/
parts:
Miriam,
Perhaps you are aware that in the LISREL model that is used by lavaan, there are not direct effects between observed variables and thus path analyses are set up as models with single-indicator latent variables.  However, lavaan will handle all of that for you behind the scenes.  It is not necessary for you to set that up in your model syntax.

If you are only interested in a path model for the observed variables, then remove the latent variables from your model and rewrite the last two lines using the observed variables.

If you are interested in used fixed unique variances to represent measurement error, then you will need to fix both the loadings (to 1, say) and the unique variances (if these are scales these can be derived from reliability estimates).  These parameters cannot be freely estimated in a model with only one indicator per latent variable.  That is the root cause of your warning.  If you choose this later option, it is good practice to conduct a sensitivity analysis by trying different values for the residual variances and comparing the results.

Keith
